name: Archduke Franz Ferdinand
kicker: Austria-Hungary’s heir · His 1914 assassination sparked World War I
briefing: Archduke Franz Ferdinand was next in line to become emperor of Austria-Hungary, a huge empire covering much of central Europe. On June 28, 1914, a Bosnian Serb nationalist named Gavrilo Princip shot him and his wife, Sophie, in the city of Sarajevo after their driver accidentally took a wrong turn. The murder set off a chain of alliances and ultimatums that exploded into World War I within weeks, and it even inspired the name of a future rock band.
answerHtml: Archduke Franz Ferdinand (or Franz Ferdinand; do not accept Franz Joseph)
accept: archduke franz ferdinand of austria hungary

trap.title: Not Franz Joseph
trap.body: Austria-Hungary had two famous Franzes: Emperor Franz Joseph I, who ruled for 68 years, and his nephew Archduke Franz Ferdinand, who was only the heir — never the emperor. Franz Joseph died of old age in 1916, two years after his nephew was assassinated. Most real quiz-bowl tossups on this material actually ask for “the assassination,” so if you’re tempted to blurt out the event, or “World War I,” instead of the person’s name, hold on one more second.
trap.fix: If the clue says “archduke,” “heir,” or “nephew,” or names Sophie, Gavrilo Princip, or the Black Hand, it’s Franz Ferdinand. If it says “emperor” and decades on the throne, that’s his uncle Franz Joseph.
